question:
Let $A=\begin{bmatrix} 3 & x & -3 \\ 2 & 5 & y \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$.

(a) Find all $x,y$ such that $|A| = 0$.

(b) For $x=0, y=2$, find the adjugate of $A$ and verify $A \cdot \mathrm{adj}(A) = |A| \cdot I$.
explanation:
(a) $|A| = 3 \begin{vmatrix}5&y\\0&2\end{vmatrix}-x\begin{vmatrix}2&y\\1&2\end{vmatrix}+(-3)\begin{vmatrix}2&5\\1&0\end{vmatrix}$

$3(5*2-0*y)=3*10=30$
$-x(2*2-1*y)=-(4-y)x$
$-3(2*0-1*5)=-3(0-5)=15$

Total: $|A|=30-(4-y)x+15=45-(4-y)x$
Set $|A|=0\implies(4-y)x=45\implies x=\frac{45}{4-y}$, $y\neq4$.

(b) Put $x=0, y=2$. Then $A=\begin{bmatrix}3&0&-3\\2&5&2\\1&0&2\end{bmatrix}$
Compute $|A|=3\begin{vmatrix}5&2\\0&2\end{vmatrix}-0+(-3)\begin{vmatrix}2&5\\1&0\end{vmatrix}=3(10-0)-3(2*0-1*5)=30-3*(-5)=30+15=45$

Calculate minors, form cofactor matrix, transpose for adjugate, then verify $A\cdot\mathrm{adj}(A)=45I$.
